'''''Elaeagnus'' × ''submacrophylla''''', formerly known as '''''Elaeagnus'' × ''ebbingei''''', is a hybrid between ''[[Elaeagnus macrophylla]]'' and ''[[Elaeagnus pungens]]''. Several [[cultivar]]s, including 'Gilt Edge', are grown in gardens as ornamental plants.<ref name=Edwa17/> Both the hybrid and 'Gilt Edge' have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHS_Es/><ref name=RHS_EsGE/>

==Description==
''Elaeagnus'' × ''submacrophylla'' is an evergreen shrub, ultimately growing to about {{cvt|4|m|ft}}. The upper surfaces of the leaves are dark green, sometimes appearing metallic; the lower surfaces are silvery and scaly. Small fragrant tubular white flowers appear in autumn.<ref name=RHS_Es/>

==Taxonomy==
The hybrid was discovered in 1929 by [[Simon Godfried Albert Doorenbos|Simon Doorenbos]], a Dutch horticulturalist, while he was director of the Parks Department in [[The Hague]]. He sowed seed from several ''Elaeagnus'' species growing next to one another. These included ''E. macrophylla'' and ''E. pungens''. Doorenbos gave the hybrid the epithet ''ebbingei'', honouring J.W.E. Ebbinge. The name ''E.'' × ''ebbingei'' was widely used until it was realized that the plant had already been described by [[Camille Servettaz]] in 1909 as ''E. submacrophylla'' – Servettaz did not realize it was a hybrid. Hence the name with [[Priority (biology)|priority]] is ''E.'' × ''submacrophylla'' and ''E.'' × ''ebbingei'' is now regarded as an [[Nomen illegitimum|illegitimate name]].<ref name=Edwa17/><ref name=IPNI_323688-1/>

==Cultivars==
[[Cultivar]]s include:<ref name=Edwa17/>
*'Albert Doorenbos' – large green leaves
*'Compacta' – dwarf plant
*'Costal Gold' – broad leaves, pale yellow in the centre when mature
*'Gilt Edge' AGM – leaves with dark green centres, golden yellow margins
*'Limelight' – leaves with yellow and pale green central areas when mature
*'The Hague' – small green leaves
